title.en: Going in, waiting and making a suggestion

summary.en: Three short expressions make the classmates’ plan easy to follow.

body.en:
In *那你怎么不先进去啊*, *先* puts entering before another possible action. The question is why the friend did not go in first. *进去* describes movement into a place.

The reply *方老师让我等你一起* explains the shared plan. *等* takes the person directly after it: wait for you. English adds for; this Mandarin line does not need an extra word between wait and you. *一起* says they will do the next thing together.

Finally, *走吧* invites the other person to leave with the speaker. *吧* gives the short action the character of a suggestion. Here *走* means let us get going, rather than specifying a particular way of walking.

These are ordinary words you can reuse when arranging to meet someone and enter a building together.
